findings.text: the artifacts line states EXIT=1 for logs/importers-head-arm.log, but that log carries no EXIT= capture line: its five chunk summaries (2, 19, 5, 16 and 7 failed) are its whole record of status. Its header also names revision 2af55ea38b, so the importer arm precedes 05cc4a25a2, the commit that moved the discard read onto promotion.discard_recorded, and therefore measures a tree other than the shipped one. The delta is behaviour-preserving (promotion.discard_recorded("") returns False, as the deleted helper did) and the node gate was re-run at head, so this is recorded rather than held.

baseline_suite cites logs/negative-control.log with exit_status 1, but that log carries no revision/tree/command header and no terminal EXIT= line: its first line is pytest output and its last is "3 failed, 2 passed in 4.88s". The three FAILED ids are present, so the negative control is admissible on its own ids, but the recorded exit status is asserted rather than captured and the log cannot be tied to the base revision from its own header.

artifacts describes logs/importers-base-failing-ids.log as "the coordinator's base run of the head-failing ids", but that log runs two unrelated tests (test_a_decline_only_round_names_its_decision_and_what_it_left and test_the_fourth_commit_is_promoted_when_every_citation_resolves) for 2 failed / EXIT=1; the 49-id base arm is logs/importers-base-arm.log (49 failed, 190 passed, EXIT=1). A reader following the citation opens evidence for a different question.

the fragment describes tests/test_a_discarded_review_never_shadows_a_promoted_one.py as holding "four cases", but the file defines five test functions: the four cases plus test_the_fixture_home_is_temporary_and_the_real_store_is_untouched. The fragment's own Measure line reports 5 passed, so the two statements disagree on the same page.
